{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693666472,"sessionID":"ses_e23eec6f2ffeNwZ9v8jq7lQHWh","part":{"id":"prt_1dc140c1a001PwQOfEnPG6D58e","messageID":"msg_1dc13e8b9001Re0uOSC33BkPPY","sessionID":"ses_e23eec6f2ffeNwZ9v8jq7lQHWh","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. From minute 86 to the end at minute 120, all four customer-facing services were at 0% errors. I don't have the final cost, but no mitigation went to a service that didn't need it.\n\n**What was broken and what I did**\n\n1. **mobile-api at 4% errors (the most expensive problem, about $730/min).** The cause was catalog-db: deploy v67, at minute -22, changed its rate limiter so the token bucket refilled 1000× too slowly, so it rejected requests with \"429 Too Many Requests\". shipping-svc passed those failures up to mobile-api. I rolled back catalog-db at minute 33.\n   - catalog-db was already near full capacity. The 30% failures during the rollback triggered retries that overloaded it, and mobile-api errors briefly hit about 55%.\n   - I rejected half of catalog-db's requests up front from minute 36 to 39 to clear the backlog, then lifted that. mobile-api was at 0% from minute 41.\n2. **partner-api at about 99% errors.** Three causes stacked up:\n   - **ranking-svc was stuck in a retry storm.** About 72% of its traffic was retries, and its real load was about 4,300 requests/s against roughly 1,950 it could handle. I found no change on it. My first attempt (rejecting 90% of requests, then lifting it) failed because the extra capacity wasn't there yet. I then scaled it from 4 to 12 replicas, rejected 70% for about 3 minutes to clear the retries, and lifted that. It has run healthy since (about 68% CPU at minute 56).\n   - **push-svc had a memory leak from deploy v25.** Its memory climbed until processes crashed and restarted, which set off its own retry storm. I rolled it back and rejected 70% of its requests during the rollback.\n   - **identity-svc got a bad deploy, v86, during the shift (minute 60).** It cut its cache key lifetime by a factor of 600 and pushed the service into overload. I rejected 70% of its requests, scaled it from 3 to 5 replicas, and rolled it back. partner-api reached 0% by minute 86.\n\n**Things I left alone**\n- cart-svc (about 25% errors) and sms-svc are alerting but no customer-facing service calls them, so they cost no revenue.\n- Other recent changes I reviewed looked harmless: shipping-svc v127 and a config change on catalog-db and on identity-svc.\n\n**Ongoing cost**\n- ranking-svc is still at 12 replicas and identity-svc at 5. Together that's $30/min above normal from when the scales finished (minutes 47 and 74).\n- I kept ranking-svc scaled up because its load is still about 4,500 requests/s and it would overload again at 4 replicas.\n- Taking identity-svc back to 3 would probably have been safe and saved about $200, but I kept the margin.\n\nSomeone should find out why ranking-svc's traffic rose from about 1,700 to about 4,500 requests/s at minute -22. Until that's understood, it can't go back to 4 replicas.","time":{"start":1794693663770,"end":1794693666461}}}
